\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঢেউ} (ḍheu)}{ঢেউ (ḍheu)}]{\bn{ঢেউ} (ḍheu) — a wave}

\label{lesson:BN-C290-dheu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a raft, then the Bengali for to be flooded.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঢেউ}}
\textbf{\bn{ঢেউ}} — \emph{ḍheu} — \textquotedblleft{}a wave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বড়} \bn{একটা} \bn{ঢেউ} \bn{এসে} \bn{নৌকাটা} \bn{উল্টে} \bn{দিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bôṛo ekṭā ḍheu ese noukāṭā ulṭe dilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A big wave came and overturned the boat.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঢেউ}} (\emph{ḍheu}) is filed in CDIAL 5580 under a Middle Indo-Aryan \emph{ḍhappa-}, 'lump', where a Bengali \emph{ḍheu}, 'a swelling', appears; how it became a wave is not set out there. It opens with \bn{ঢ}, the breathy \emph{ḍh}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍheu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍheu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôṛo ekṭā ḍheu ese noukāṭā ulṭe dilô.} — A big wave came and overturned the boat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a raft, then the Bengali for to be flooded, then say \emph{ḍheu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ঢেউ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wave\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{তীর} (tīr)}{তীর (tīr)}]{\bn{তীর} (tīr) — a riverbank; a shore}

\label{lesson:BN-C290-tir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to be flooded, then the Bengali for a wave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{তীর}}
\textbf{\bn{তীর}} — \emph{tīr} — \textquotedblleft{}a riverbank; a shore\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঢেউ} \bn{নৌকাটাকে} \bn{তীরে} \bn{নিয়ে} \bn{এল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍheu noukāṭāke tīre niye elô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The waves carried the boat to the shore.
\end{quote}

A second \bn{তীর}, an arrow, is a different word.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{তীর}} (\emph{tīr}) is Sanskrit \emph{tīra}, 'a shore, a bank' (Monier-Williams), unchanged. \bn{নদীর} \bn{তীরে}, on the riverbank.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tīr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍheu noukāṭāke tīre niye elô.} — The waves carried the boat to the shore.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to be flooded, then the Bengali for a wave, then say \emph{tīr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{তীর} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A riverbank; a shore\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভাঙন} (bhāngôn)}{ভাঙন (bhāngôn)}]{\bn{ভাঙন} (bhāngôn) — the eating away of a riverbank; erosion}

\label{lesson:BN-C290-bhangon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a wave, then the Bengali for a riverbank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভাঙন}}
\textbf{\bn{ভাঙন}} — \emph{bhāngôn} — \textquotedblleft{}the eating away of a riverbank; erosion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{নদীর} \bn{ভাঙনে} \bn{গ্রামের} \bn{স্কুলটা} \bn{নদীতে} \bn{চলে} \bn{গেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nôdīr bhāngône grāmer skulṭā nôdīte chôle gelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The river ate away its bank and the village school went into the water.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভাঙন}} (\emph{bhāngôn}) is \textbf{\bn{ভাঙা}}, to break — CDIAL 9353, Sanskrit \emph{bhaṅga} — with the -\bn{ন} ending that names the act: the breaking away of a riverbank, a word the river delta needs.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhāngôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhāngôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nôdīr bhāngône grāmer skulṭā nôdīte chôle gelô.} — The river ate away its bank and the village school went into the water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a wave, then the Bengali for a riverbank, then say \emph{bhāngôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ভাঙন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The eating away of a riverbank; erosion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{গৃহহীন} (grihôhīn)}{গৃহহীন (grihôhīn)}]{\bn{গৃহহীন} (grihôhīn) — homeless}

\label{lesson:BN-C290-grihohin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a riverbank, then the Bengali for erosion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{গৃহহীন}}
\textbf{\bn{গৃহহীন}} — \emph{grihôhīn} — \textquotedblleft{}homeless\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বন্যার} \bn{পরে} \bn{অনেক} \bn{পরিবার} \bn{গৃহহীন} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bônyār pôre ônek pôribār grihôhīn hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the flood many families were left homeless.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{গৃহহীন}} (\emph{grihôhīn}) joins Sanskrit \emph{gṛha}, 'a house, a home', to \emph{hīna}, 'left, deprived of' (Monier-Williams): without a house. It is a word of the news more than of talk.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grihôhīn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grihôhīn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bônyār pôre ônek pôribār grihôhīn hôlô.} — After the flood many families were left homeless.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a riverbank, then the Bengali for erosion, then say \emph{grihôhīn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{গৃহহীন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Homeless\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হেলিকপ্টার} (helikôpṭār)}{হেলিকপ্টার (helikôpṭār)}]{\bn{হেলিকপ্টার} (helikôpṭār) — a helicopter}

\label{lesson:BN-C290-helikoptar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for erosion, then the Bengali for homeless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হেলিকপ্টার}}
\textbf{\bn{হেলিকপ্টার}} — \emph{helikôpṭār} — \textquotedblleft{}a helicopter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সেনাবাহিনীর} \bn{হেলিকপ্টার} \bn{ছাদ} \bn{থেকে} \bn{মানুষ} \bn{তুলল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{senābāhinīr helikôpṭār chhād theke mānush tullô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Army helicopters lifted people off the rooftops.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{হেলিকপ্টার}} (\emph{helikôpṭār}) is English \emph{helicopter}, built in the nineteenth century from Greek words for 'spiral' and 'wing'.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
